problem: Existing EQA benchmarks cover small, simple household scenes and do not test multi-scale reasoning over many real images, cited visual evidence, or agreement with expert ratings. The strongest EM-EQA baseline, Multi-Frame VLM, feeds all images into one long context, where it suffers from positional bias (lost in the middle).
motivation: Bridge inspection offers real expert-annotated data: reports with egocentric photos, inspector notes and standardized NBI 0-9 ratings. Inspectors must justify ratings with photographic evidence, so a benchmark should also score which images a model cites. The authors hypothesize that long-context positional bias hurts Multi-Frame VLM, and that letting an agent selectively retrieve images would help.
key_idea: Turn episodic-memory EQA into an active navigation problem: build an image-node scene graph with a VLM and let a VLM agent traverse it in an MDP (Move/Compare/Reason/Respond) to pull only relevant images into context.
insight: Making the agent retrieve images on demand improves condition-rating accuracy, image-citation relevance and answer correctness over feeding all images at once, especially with Grok 4 Fast. Appendix heatmaps show that all methods degrade as node/edge counts grow, but EMVR degrades less, consistent with mitigating lost-in-the-middle. Scene-graph context alone helps the baselines too (Multi-Frame VLM w/ SG beats plain Multi-Frame VLM), so part of the gain comes from the graph rather than navigation. The gain is not uniform across VLMs: EMVR is not best on Answer Correctness with Gemini Flash Lite.
method: BridgeEQA dataset: 2,200 open-vocabulary QA pairs over 200 Vermont VTrans bridge inspection reports, 9,586 images, split 1,100 train / 1,100 test. Built by filtering reports (>=20 images), then using Gemini 2.5 Flash/Pro to parse text, image references and NBI ratings, and to generate QAs, followed by automated and human validation.

Image-based scene graph: a VLM (Gemini 2.5 Flash, falling back to Gemini 2.5 Pro) outputs JSON nodes, one per image, with central focus, description and natural-language directed edges (hierarchical, structural, adjacency, condition similarity, membership). Construction needs no GPS or metadata.
EMVR MDP: the state is the current node plus interaction history. The agent starts with only the scene graph (labels, descriptions, edges), not the images.

Actions via function calls: Move(v_j) to a neighbor, Compare({v_i,v_j,...}) loads 2 or more images, Reason(v_i) does self-questioning on one image, Respond(q) returns the answer, cited images and condition rating.
EMVR variants: 'SG Only' starts with the graph text only; 'Images + SG' also gives the images at the start.
Condition rating accuracy: exact match and within +-1 of the expert NBI rating.

Image citation relevance metric: Gemini 2.5 Flash acts as VLM judge comparing agent-cited images with reference images (scores 0-1, penalizing citing more than 5x the reference count). Spearman correlation with 3 human annotators is 0.817.

setting.backbone: Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Grok 4 Fast (frozen, prompted); appendix: Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking, Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B, Nemotron-3 Nano-30B-A3B
setting.training_data: none (training-free; a 1,100-QA train split exists but is not used to train the method)
setting.observation: unordered set of real egocentric inspection photos per bridge (avg ~48 images) plus a VLM-generated scene graph with text descriptions
setting.action_space: function calls over an image scene graph: Move to neighbor node, Compare multiple images, Reason on one image, Respond
setting.simulator: none (offline image collections from real inspection reports)

numbers_note: Condition rating accuracy (exact and within +-1) for the main models is given only in a figure, so no values are extracted. Text says EMVR improves +-1 accuracy by 9.34 pp, Image Citation Relevance by 20.2 pp and Answer Correctness by 7.2 pp over Multi-Frame VLM with Grok 4 Fast. Open-source results in the appendix use a subset of scenes with fewer than 30 images and are not comparable to the main results, so they are omitted here.
results: With Grok 4 Fast, EMVR w/ Images + SG reaches Answer Correctness 0.648 and Image Citation Relevance 0.889, versus 0.576 and 0.687 for Multi-Frame VLM. The strongest non-navigational baseline with scene graph, Multi-Frame VLM w/ SG, scores 0.622 and 0.833. Gains vary by model: with Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite, Multi-Frame VLM w/ SG has the best Answer Correctness (0.581), although EMVR is best on citation relevance (0.849).
limitations: Sub-30B open-source VLMs could not reliably follow structured-output and function-calling formats and have small context windows, so they were tested only on scenes with fewer than 30 images.

The dataset, QA pairs, scene graphs and metric judge are all produced by Gemini and Grok-family LLMs, and the benchmark covers only Vermont bridges from one agency, which risks bias and limits generality.

The scene graph is built from full-context VLM calls, so it inherits the long-context issue and adds cost; the hypothesis that positional bias explains the baseline gap is supported only indirectly by the node/edge heatmaps.
